messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sustained p99 > 6s for /v1/generate on hotshot-dedicated eu-west-1. Queue depth rising (1.1k -> 1.4k), warmup_failures=42 in last 5m. Paging: @maria-oncall @josh-sre @sahil.ops
maria-oncall: acknowledged. Brief status: are we seeing classic cold-warmup churn or actual GPU saturation? Any customer-visible timeouts yet?
josh-sre: pulling infra logs. Autoscaler shows rapid up/down events starting ~10:52 -> 10:59, nodes frequently not finishing warmup before scale-down, causing backlog to build. I see scale_up +20 then scale_down -20 multiple times.
sahil.ops: application metrics: EU p95 jumped 180ms -> 900ms; p99 ~6.2s. A few streaming sessions reported stalls (clients sending keepalive). Support queue has two urgent tickets referencing generation timeouts.
maria-oncall: marking P1. @liz-product can you confirm enterprise impact and notify support? @nora-eng we may need immediate fallback routing.
liz-product: confirming two enterprise tenants in EU with timeouts; support alerted, customers waiting for ETA. Drafting a short note now.
nora-eng: propose immediate mitigation: divert 35% of new /v1/generate traffic to hotshot-fallback-eu (quantized low-latency variant) and perform a manual resize of pool to add capacity while we stabilize autoscaler config. Fallback quality loss is small, acceptable for short window.
josh-sre: +1 for manual resize. Autoscaler seems overly aggressive on scale_down; cooldown too short and scale_rate is high. Recommend set cooldown 300s and max_scale_rate=0.25 for hotshot-eu.
sahil.ops: I can flip autoscaler params, but manual add will be faster. @deploy-bot can you open manual-resize: +18 nodes hotshot-eu, hold 12m?
deploy-bot: manual-resize initiated: +18 nodes to hotshot-eu. ETA ~70s. Runbook tag: hotshot-warmup-throttle.
observability-bot: metric snapshot: queue_depth=1402 -> 1320 (immediate), p99=6.2s. Noting KV_cold_hit_rate is high for new nodes.
maria-oncall: while nodes are provisioning, reduce scale churn: @sahil.ops set autoscaler.cooldown=300 and max_scale_rate=0.25 for hotshot-eu. Also enable a short warmup hold (traffic gating) for newly attached nodes.
sahil.ops: done: autoscaler.cooldown=300; autoscaler.max_scale_rate=0.25. Enabling node warmup gating (traffic_hold=30s) for hotshot-eu.
josh-sre: traffic gating should help. Also suggest optimistic KV prefill for expected top prefixes for the next 10m. I can run a one-off job to preseed KV on the new nodes.
sahil.ops: launching kv-prefill-job: top200-prefixes -> targeting hotshot-eu new nodes. Job started.
nora-eng: routing change: smart-router override applied: /v1/generate -> hotshot-fallback-eu 35% immediate. Adding note: fallback is quantized; flag to support.
liz-product: support message sent to affected customers noting degraded latency and fallback routing; asking for permission to apply mitigation (customers acknowledged).
observability-bot: 90s after mitigation: queue_depth=420, p95=380ms, p99=1.7s. Streaming_stalls reduced from 0.12/min -> 0.02/min.
maria-oncall: good signal. Keep manual nodes live for 12m, monitor. Capture warmup handshake failures (why nodes not finish warmup previously).
josh-sre: digging into warmup handshake logs: many nodes hit timeout waiting for KV seed and model init due to a race with prewarm job. We should detect nodes that never pass warmup and avoid counting them as ready.
sahil.ops: enabling "exclude-if-warmup-fails" for the scale group and increasing warmup timeout to 120s. Also enabling sticky session routing for overflow queue so in-flight sessions are routed to warmed nodes when possible.
nora-eng: flipping sticky routing for overflow queue ON for 10m. This pins ~20% of sessions to warmed nodes.
observability-bot: sticky binding observed ~21% of active sessions. streaming_stalls trending down. p99 stable ~1.5s.
maria-oncall: can we start draining the short-lived scale-down events historically? Need a post-incident action to add hysteresis.
josh-sre: noted. Immediate checklist: 1) hold manual resize for 12m (done), 2) keep fallback routing 35% while queue_depth > 500 or p99 > 3s, 3) track warmup-failure count and exclude nodes that fail init.
sahil.ops: I'll open a PR to make default autoscaler.cooldown 180s for hotshot pools and add a hysteresis param to avoid flapping on brief spikes. Assign to infra-team.
liz-product: customer comms updated; two customers said they will accept fallback for short period, asking for postmortem once done.
maria-oncall: any remaining streaming stalls on long-token sessions?
josh-sre: a few outliers for tokens > 1024 still show latency ~3-4s, likely KV cold hits in long contexts. We should prefetch more prefixes for sessions that grow beyond token threshold.
nora-eng: consider progressive warmup: bring node to 50% traffic for first 2 minutes then full traffic if warmup healthy. Add to routing playbook.
maria-oncall: agreed. Postmortem owners: incident writeup -> me. Autoscaler tuning PR -> @sahil.ops. Routing/runbook updates -> @nora-eng. Customer follow-up -> @liz-product.
sahil.ops: PR opened: increase cooldown + hysteresis param, link: https://r.git/internal/pr/2345
nora-eng: updating runbook now: add step for immediate fallback + sticky routing when queue_depth>800 and p99>4s. Also doc progressive warmup.
observability-bot: final snapshot at T+10m: queue_depth=380, p95=310ms, p99=1.4s, streaming_stalls low.
maria-oncall: incident mitigated. Keeping open for postmortem. Handoff to overnight watch: @sleeping-oncall will monitor autoscaler logs and p99.
sleeping-oncall: ack. I'll watch for any autoscaler flaps and re-open if queue_depth spikes or p99 > 3s.
maria-oncall: thanks team :thumbsup: 
---
Post-incident action items captured in thread for follow-up:
- Improve detection of warmup-failed nodes and exclude them from ready pool (owner: josh-sre)
- Autoscaler defaults: cooldown bump + hysteresis (owner: sahil.ops)
- Progressive warmup traffic gating and routing playbook (owner: nora-eng)
- KV prefetch strategy for top prefixes and long-token sessions (owner: eng-ml)
- Update support templates & SLA communication (owner: liz-product)
End of thread.
